newsitem.title: YEMEN: Speedy release seen for Polish hostages in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Speedy release seen for Polish hostages in Yemen.

text.p: Negotiations to free five Polish tourists held hostage by tribesmen in the mountains of Yemen were progressing well and their release was expected soon, the Polish ambassador to Yemen said on Sunday.
The tourists -- three men and two women between the ages of 50 and 64 -- were abducted on their way to archaeological sites in eastern Yemen last week and were initially thought to be Dutch.
"We received official notification from the (Yemeni) interior ministry today (Sunday) that the kidnapped people are Polish," Ambassador Krzyfztof Suprowicz told Reuters.
"They told us negotiations are still continuing with the kidnappers and they affirmed that an imminent release will take place," he said.
Suprowicz said he had no further details.
"All we are concerned about is...that the Yemeni authorities reach a peaceful settlement of this problem soon," he said.
The tourists were abducted by members of the Al al-Masni tribe in the Khawlan area, about 65 km (40 miles) east of the capital Sanaa.
The kidnapping, the second involving European holidaymakers this month, took place sometime between Tuesday and Thursday, diplomats said.
On Friday, the tribesmen fired rocket-propelled grenades at military forces who had surrounded them, killing three soldiers and wounding five.
Diplomats said villagers had also been wounded, but said they had received confirmation the hostages were unharmed.
Officials said the military siege was continuing.
Yemeni authorities on December 19 freed five Dutch tourists who were abducted and briefly held by tribesmen while touring an area 240 km (150 miles) north of Sanaa.

In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or other foreigners to use as bargaining chips. The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political.
The current standoff is the first kidnapping involving the Al al-Masni tribe, which lives in the Beni Jabr area near Khawlan.
